值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解 Analogue Pocket 如何以 FPGA 硬體模擬，讓經典掌機卡帶重新遊玩。
  • 看見復古遊戲體驗如何結合高解析度螢幕、畫面濾鏡與現代功能。
  • 認識 Logitech MX Master 3S Developer Edition 的開發者主題設計與趣味彩蛋。
  • 從作者的實際使用與購買考量，了解兩款產品各自適合哪些玩家與使用者。

摘要

本月新玩具開箱

Ah Hui 以「Super Spender」為名，分享本月購入的四項產品，並說明每件商品吸引他的原因，以及實際入手後是否值得。影片預告的品項包括復古掌機 Analogue Pocket、開發者限定版 Logitech 滑鼠、Soundcore 真無線耳機，以及初音未來與水月雨聯名的 MAGE 無線耳機；接著先從 Analogue Pocket 開始介紹。

Analogue Pocket：讓童年卡帶重回日常

Ah Hui 表示，自己多年來一直留意 Analogue Pocket（AP），但它價格不低，官方售價超過兩百美元，市面購入也可能要價上萬元新台幣。考量到收藏與改裝舊掌機同樣需要花費，他最後決定入手。AP 的特色是採用雙 FPGA，以硬體層級重現遊戲主機的運作方式，與一般透過軟體模擬遊戲的平價掌機不同；機身還設有卡帶插槽，可直接遊玩 Game Boy、Game Boy Color 與 GBA 原版卡帶。

Ah Hui 示範插入自己喜愛的《星之卡比 夢之泉物語 2》卡帶，形容把收藏多年的卡帶接上新世代掌機、立刻啟動遊戲，彷彿讓童年記憶重新活了過來。AP 的 3.5 吋螢幕解析度為 1600×1440，像素密度達 615 PPI，並以像素對應方式放大畫面；玩家還能切換不同世代掌機的顯示質感，模擬像素格、背光液晶與子像素排列等效果。

除了原生支援 GB、GBC 與 GBA，AP 的 OpenFPGA 平台也讓第三方開發者能模擬其他系統，另有卡帶轉接器可支援 Game Gear、Atari Lynx、Neo Geo Pocket 等主機。它具備約 4300mAh 電池，遊玩時間約 6 至 10 小時，並提供 microSD、USB-C、立體聲喇叭、耳機孔、連結線接口與影像輸出等功能，也支援存檔狀態、遊戲截圖及外接控制器。

Ah Hui 認為，AP 並非追求低價、方便大量遊玩盜版或模擬遊戲的產品，而是適合珍惜原版卡帶、重視硬體還原與收藏體驗的玩家。他購買它的主要原因，是讓原本收在抽屜裡的童年卡帶能重新拿起來遊玩；多年等待後，第一次插入卡帶的滿足感，正是這筆花費對他而言最值得之處。

Logitech MX Master 3S Developer Edition

第二項產品是 Logitech MX Master 3S Developer Edition。Ah Hui 平常已使用標準版，因此不再重複介紹觸覺回饋、人體工學、8000 DPI 感應器、電池續航、滾輪與 Logi Options+ 自訂功能。這款開發者限定版的硬體與功能和一般版相同，主要差異在於外觀與配件融入軟體開發文化：滑鼠上有程式碼片段、電路板走線、CNC 加工質感與立體視覺效果，並以灰、白、黑搭配螢光綠，呈現如開發工作室工具般的風格。

滑鼠上的細節藏有不少程式設計彩蛋，例如代表程式執行的「Play」圖示、常見的雙斜線註解符號，以及程式入門者熟悉的「HelloWorld」；「0x100」則以十六進位形式指向 256，呼應工程師文化。底部還印有原版推出日期，並加入與 4 月 1 日相關的文字玩笑。Ah Hui 認為，這些元素並非只放大品牌標誌，而是將開發者主題融入整體設計。

台灣購買此限定版還能獲得專屬黑卡一套，每張都有 TW001 至 TW400 的獨立序號，總數僅 400 套；全球限量則為 50,000 支，官方表示不會再版。影片提到產品預計於 12 月 28 日正式上市，並在介紹完限量資訊後，尚未進一步交代這款滑鼠的購買結論。

摘要

本月新玩具開箱

Ah Hui 以「Super Spender」為名，分享本月購入的四項產品，並說明每件商品吸引他的原因，以及實際入手後是否值得。影片預告的品項包括復古掌機 Analogue Pocket、開發者限定版 Logitech 滑鼠、Soundcore 真無線耳機，以及初音未來與水月雨聯名的 MAGE 無線耳機；接著先從 Analogue Pocket 開始介紹。

Analogue Pocket：讓童年卡帶重回日常

Ah Hui 表示，自己多年來一直留意 Analogue Pocket（AP），但它價格不低，官方售價超過兩百美元，市面購入也可能要價上萬元新台幣。考量到收藏與改裝舊掌機同樣需要花費，他最後決定入手。AP 的特色是採用雙 FPGA，以硬體層級重現遊戲主機的運作方式，與一般透過軟體模擬遊戲的平價掌機不同；機身還設有卡帶插槽，可直接遊玩 Game Boy、Game Boy Color 與 GBA 原版卡帶。

Ah Hui 示範插入自己喜愛的《星之卡比 夢之泉物語 2》卡帶，形容把收藏多年的卡帶接上新世代掌機、立刻啟動遊戲，彷彿讓童年記憶重新活了過來。AP 的 3.5 吋螢幕解析度為 1600×1440，像素密度達 615 PPI，並以像素對應方式放大畫面；玩家還能切換不同世代掌機的顯示質感，模擬像素格、背光液晶與子像素排列等效果。

除了原生支援 GB、GBC 與 GBA，AP 的 OpenFPGA 平台也讓第三方開發者能模擬其他系統，另有卡帶轉接器可支援 Game Gear、Atari Lynx、Neo Geo Pocket 等主機。它具備約 4300mAh 電池，遊玩時間約 6 至 10 小時，並提供 microSD、USB-C、立體聲喇叭、耳機孔、連結線接口與影像輸出等功能，也支援存檔狀態、遊戲截圖及外接控制器。

Ah Hui 認為，AP 並非追求低價、方便大量遊玩盜版或模擬遊戲的產品，而是適合珍惜原版卡帶、重視硬體還原與收藏體驗的玩家。他購買它的主要原因，是讓原本收在抽屜裡的童年卡帶能重新拿起來遊玩；多年等待後，第一次插入卡帶的滿足感，正是這筆花費對他而言最值得之處。

Logitech MX Master 3S Developer Edition

第二項產品是 Logitech MX Master 3S Developer Edition。Ah Hui 平常已使用標準版，因此不再重複介紹觸覺回饋、人體工學、8000 DPI 感應器、電池續航、滾輪與 Logi Options+ 自訂功能。這款開發者限定版的硬體與功能和一般版相同，主要差異在於外觀與配件融入軟體開發文化：滑鼠上有程式碼片段、電路板走線、CNC 加工質感與立體視覺效果，並以灰、白、黑搭配螢光綠，呈現如開發工作室工具般的風格。

滑鼠上的細節藏有不少程式設計彩蛋，例如代表程式執行的「Play」圖示、常見的雙斜線註解符號，以及程式入門者熟悉的「HelloWorld」；「0x100」則以十六進位形式指向 256，呼應工程師文化。底部還印有原版推出日期，並加入與 4 月 1 日相關的文字玩笑。Ah Hui 認為，這些元素並非只放大品牌標誌，而是將開發者主題融入整體設計。

台灣購買此限定版還能獲得專屬黑卡一套，每張都有 TW001 至 TW400 的獨立序號，總數僅 400 套；全球限量則為 50,000 支，官方表示不會再版。影片提到產品預計於 12 月 28 日正式上市，並在介紹完限量資訊後，尚未進一步交代這款滑鼠的購買結論。

摘要

摺疊手機類型與 iPhone 的定位

作者表示，自己使用過三十多款摺疊手機，因此這次不只開箱，也會以長期使用者的角度檢視蘋果的首次嘗試。他先將市場上的摺疊手機分成幾類：主打輕巧與趣味操作的上下翻蓋型、展開後兼具手機與平板用途的書本式大摺疊，以及藉由兩個轉軸帶來更大螢幕、但通常更厚重昂貴的三摺疊。此外，還有螢幕比例較寬、較接近平板形狀的寬幅摺疊。

這款 iPhone 採用寬幅大摺疊設計，合起時為 5.4 吋外螢幕，展開後則是 7.6 吋的小型平板。作者將它視為蘋果風格的寬幅摺疊機，而非小型翻蓋手機或單純放大的 iPhone。

機身規格與螢幕特色

機身提供星光白與夜空黑兩種顏色，容量從 256GB 到 2TB。外觀採用鈦金屬邊框與轉軸外蓋，搭配不同世代的 Ceramic Shield，並具備 IP68 防塵防水能力。手機展開厚度為 5.2 毫米、摺疊厚度為 11.3 毫米，重量 254 克；作者認為展開時相當纖薄，但收起後的厚度與重量放在口袋裡會很有存在感。

內外螢幕皆支援最高 120Hz ProMotion，戶外峰值亮度可達 3000 尼特。內螢幕採用 Super Retina XDR 可摺疊 OLED 面板，解析度為 1878 × 2670。作者特別提到螢幕上的奈米紋理霧面處理，但澄清這項效果是透過原廠預先貼上的保護貼實現，而非直接蝕刻在摺疊面板上。

霧面保護貼與摺痕表現

作者認為霧面螢幕較不易反光，長時間閱讀文章、漫畫或瀏覽網頁時相當舒適；不過，觀看暗色影片時，黑色可能不如亮面螢幕深邃，對比感也較弱，因此霧面與亮面各有適合的內容情境。

原廠保護貼讓中央摺痕在視覺上幾乎難以察覺，作者稱其摺痕表現非常出色，甚至可說是目前頂尖水準之一。雖然關閉螢幕並從斜角觀看時，仍看得到結構變化，手指也能摸到輕微隆起，但螢幕亮起後看影片、照片或瀏覽網頁，摺痕很容易被忽略。作者提醒，若內螢幕保護貼翹起，應立即聯絡原廠更換，不建議一般使用者自行撕除或更換，以免受力不均增加螢幕損壞風險。

隱藏式鏡頭與解鎖方式

內螢幕前鏡頭採用螢幕下鏡頭技術，正面觀看時隱藏得相當自然，閱讀、看影片或玩遊戲時能維持完整的沉浸感。作者原本擔心蘋果會限制內螢幕自拍功能，但實際上自拍畫質不差，也能正常使用。

摺疊手機類型與 iPhone 的定位

作者表示，自己使用過三十多款摺疊手機，因此這次不只開箱，也會以長期使用者的角度檢視蘋果的首次嘗試。他先將市場上的摺疊手機分成幾類：主打輕巧與趣味操作的上下翻蓋型、展開後兼具手機與平板用途的書本式大摺疊，以及藉由兩個轉軸帶來更大螢幕、但通常更厚重昂貴的三摺疊。此外，還有螢幕比例較寬、較接近平板形狀的寬幅摺疊。

這款 iPhone 採用寬幅大摺疊設計，合起時為 5.4 吋外螢幕，展開後則是 7.6 吋的小型平板。作者將它視為蘋果風格的寬幅摺疊機，而非小型翻蓋手機或單純放大的 iPhone。

霧面保護貼與摺痕表現

# 折痕到底藏得多好？

approach; it's actually a form of screen technology. The protector is part of its panel technology, and I even think it’s a very reasonable and well-executed solution that other manufacturers could learn from. But I still need to be clear: it doesn't mean there is absolutely no crease. If you turn off the screen and look at it from a sharp angle, you can still see the structural change, and you can feel a slight bump with your finger; that will still be there. However, once the screen is on, when you’re watching videos, viewing photos, or scrolling through web pages, the crease is very easy to overlook. Right, did everyone notice something? Did you see it?

# UDC 螢幕下鏡頭與自拍體驗

What’s missing here? Yes, exactly. The inner camera uses under-display camera (UDC) technology. Aside from the fact that the nano-treatment on the screen protector has to avoid the camera area, which causes some light reflections from different angles, when you face it directly, the camera is hidden incredibly well. If no one told you, you would find it very hard to even notice its existence. When the camera isn't in use, it stays hidden. Whether you're reading, watching videos , or gaming, the level of immersion is maxed out; it’s really satisfying. And the image quality for inner-screen selfies is actually quite decent. Actually, before it launched, and even before I got my hands on it, I was constantly wondering if Apple would lock the UDC selfie function. Turns out the quality is pretty good, and Apple didn't disable the feature, so you can still use the inner screen to take selfies. Since folding phones have both inner and outer screen usage scenarios, the iPhone, like most other brands ' foldables, uses side-mounted fingerprint recognition, integrating Touch ID into the power button on the side. So, I have to mention that it.

# Touch ID 與 eSIM 使用注意

does not have Face ID. For Apple users, since the iPhone X, you’re likely very accustomed to the experience of Face ID—picking it up to unlock, and having it recognize you automatically. Switching back to using my finger on the side button feels a bit sluggish at first, I really do feel that way. Since you pick up a foldable phone in different orientations, I suggest registering fingers from both your left and right hands; I’ve registered my left index finger, and my right thumb and index finger. You can set it up according to your needs, and the benefit is that whether it’s on the. table or in your hand, in any scenario, a quick touch is all it takes to unlock . But I have to say, since it only has Touch ID and doesn't offer face unlock or even iris scanning, that’s a bit of a shame. Also, note that the global version of the iPhone Fold only supports eSIM, so there is no physical SIM tray. It can store multiple eSIMs, and you can run two at once for dual-SIM functionality, but once you get it, you'll still need to visit your carrier to switch over your number. The next key point, which might even be more important than the hardware, is that for a foldable, it’s not just.

# iOS 多工、App 雙開與遊戲玩法

about the build, but whether it’s actually useful once unfolded. This iPhone Fold runs on a redesigned iOS 17 , where you can use split-view mode to display two apps side-by-side on the inner screen. Currently, it supports side-by-side display in landscape mode; you can have your photo app on the left and mail on the right, dragging photos directly into emails, or even open two windows of the same app, which is very practical for work. You can have an email open on one side and Excel on the other to organize data, or if you need to reply to messages while checking. reports, this split-screen method is much smoother than constantly switching apps on a regular iPhone. If the app supports it, you can even open two instances of the same program, and apps like Safari already support this. You can have one webpage open on the left and another on the right, checking product specs while looking at prices, or researching hotels while viewing maps and flight info. For users who need to look up information and multitask, this large-screen productivity is truly convenient, and it’s the main reason I’ve been using foldable phones for so many years . Even in gaming, you can apply this method for more ways to play. For. example, you can open Pikmin on the left and Pokémon on the right. That’s right, it’s super awesome— a total nerd’s dream come true. You can also have a game running on one side while looking up a strategy guide on the other. With the iPhone Du’s large unfolded screen, running two games or apps at once isn't just cool and flashy; it’s genuinely practical, spacious, and great for multitasking. I feel that the difference between foldables and tablets isn't just about having a bigger screen. If you only wanted a larger display, you’d just pick a tablet; you already have a big screen there, but foldables are different. You get the portability of a. phone combined with a massive internal screen and more versatile multitasking workflows, all packed into one pocketable device. It's super. Beyond just app multitasking, many features unique to foldables have also appeared on the iPhone. For example, you can leave it half-folded on a table. If the app supports it, like the camera or video player, it has a dedicated interface that splits automatically. You can stand it up for video calls or just leave it on the desk to use the StandBy clock feature. That's right,.

# 半摺模式與 StandBy 桌面時鐘

the most expensive desk clock ever. Perhaps because of the larger screen, this iPhone Du is the first iPhone to natively support a stylus; the Apple Pencil USB-C is supported on the iPhone Du. And it's not just for the inner screen when unfolded; both the inner and outer displays support the Apple Pencil, which is actually very rare to see right now. Whether it's the iPhone Du’s outer screen when folded or the 7.6-inch large screen when opened, you can use it for taking notes, drawing, or marking up content. You can quickly jot down an idea on the outer screen, then open it up to organize it on the big display, or use it to annotate photos, documents, and emails. So this.

# Apple Pencil 支援與功能限制

Apple Pencil utility isn't just for tablet mode; it works in both folded and unfolded states. However, it is a bit of a pity that there are still a few drawbacks. The first is that it only supports the Apple Pencil USB-C version, which lacks pressure sensitivity. So, when you draw lines, you won't get the variable line thickness you'd see with the Apple Pencil Pro. If you're a professional artist or designer with those advanced needs, that’s definitely a downside. Also, the official announcement stated this feature would launch later this year and wouldn't support floating windows. However, you can already get a sneak peek in the current open beta. If. you have it, you can update and use it right now, so I think it's coming along very quickly and should be available to everyone soon. However, this brings up a more realistic issue, which is the optimization of apps; the level of support still takes time. For now, Apple's own apps or those that have already been updated make full use of both the inner and outer screen space. But some older apps might still show black bars or appear in a windowed format. You can try to force full screen, but it’s not perfect. Plus,.

# App 適配、黑邊與軟體生態

because the UI has been moved to the right side, there will inevitably be some black bars. Take common apps: Facebook supports it, but X doesn't. Nvidia supports it, but Disney + doesn't. This just goes to show that it still takes time. So, as it stands, the iPhone Duo has hardware that is already complete, while the software ecosystem is playing catch-up for a foldable. Personally, having used many foldables, I believe Apple has much stronger leverage over app developers. Look at Facebook; it’s been six years and support is still incomplete. Six years. —do you know how painful that journey has been? It just doesn't support it; it resets every time you open it. But when Apple enters the scene, the Apple version of Facebook is ready from day one. Isn't that great? Facebook, please hurry up and update already! Even now, opening and closing it still requires a refresh. Regarding the camera, the iPhone Duo uses a 48-megapixel dual-fusion camera system with a main lens and an ultra-wide lens. The main 48-megapixel lens supports sensor-shift optical image stabilization and can achieve 2x optical-quality zoom. However, it lacks a dedicated telephoto.

# 相機規格與沒有獨立長焦的取捨

lens. This 2x zoom is based on cropping the high-resolution main sensor; it isn't the true, dedicated telephoto found on the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, so the zoom still falls a bit short. Also, since it's not a "Pro" model, it naturally lacks Pro controls and doesn't feature the latest variable aperture found on the 18 Pro Max. So, if I had to define its camera tier using a model everyone is familiar with , I’d say the overall hardware capability of the iPhone Duo is roughly on par with the standard iPhone 17. Simply put, if your daily photography needs are met by a flagship-level main lens, ultra-wide angle, and video capabilities, this is for you. However,. it’s not a complete camera system like the Pro models that include telephoto lenses or variable apertures. But its video capabilities are still very strong; the main lens supports 4K at a world-leading 120 FPS, and it also supports dual-camera simultaneous recording. The main, really the main focus of the iPhone, lies in the new features unique to its foldable form factor. For example, its dual-screen preview feature allows the person being photographed to see your composition directly through the outer display. In practice, when you're using the rear camera to take photos of someone else, they don't just have to stand there waiting for you to hit the shutter. They can check the outer screen to see if they're fully in the frame, if their.

# 雙面預覽：被拍的人也能看構圖

expression is natural, or if their pose or the composition needs adjusting. That's right, I'm talking about that boyfriend or husband of yours who really can't take a decent photo; this feature will be an absolute lifesaver for you. You can ensure that while you're being photographed, you can see the screen yourself to confirm the composition is perfect before the other person presses the shutter. Whether you're taking family portraits, shooting outfit photos for friends, or using the main camera for portraits, this function is super useful. Now, there's another handy feature: Smart Capture. Do other phones have something similar? The closest thing seems to be gesture-activated countdown timers, but.

# 智慧拍攝：合照不用追倒數計時

this Smart Capture takes it a step further. You can stand the iPhone up on a table, turn on Smart Capture, and just fix the composition. You don't have to run back to the phone to hit the shutter, and you don't have to worry about when the countdown timer will go off. The phone automatically recognizes the people in the frame. Once everyone is in the shot and ready, it will complete the photo automatically. This is incredibly convenient for group photos, where the problem is often that someone isn't standing right or is adjusting their clothes when the timer goes off. Now, it detects when you change poses, so. you don't have to keep running back and forth. You won't have to wait until after the shot to realize someone blinked or wasn't looking at the camera . Every time someone changes their pose —like a peace sign or a shift in position—it captures a shot automatically. It's fully automatic and super convenient. Other brands should take notes, especially since it can be propped up on a table now; you don't even need a tripod. This really isn't just adding photography features to a regular phone; it's about utilizing the device's inherent folding form factor. Next, similar to the outer screen camera function mentioned earlier, there is also a feature called "Look Here." The "Look Here" feature uses the.

# 看看鏡頭與雙面 FaceTime

outer screen to display animations, effectively attracting children to look toward the camera. This "Look at the Camera" feature addresses the most common problem when photographing kids: they often don't look at the lens when you hold the phone, or the more you tell them to look here, the more they look elsewhere. This "Look at the Camera" feature shows cute animated visual prompts on the outer screen, so when kids see something on the other side of the phone, their gaze naturally shifts toward the camera lens. There really should be a cat-teaser function for taking photos of my cat. There are plenty of other features too, like support for two-way FaceTime, allowing. friends to interact and talk together. If I were to evaluate the iPhone Duo, its overall camera capability is close to the iPhone 17 base model, plus the unique ways of playing that only a foldable phone offers. Honestly speaking, it’s true that it doesn't have the most luxurious camera specs among current foldables, but it knows how to use the folding screen to solve issues like selfies, group photos, and including yourself in shots, bringing some unique Apple ingenuity. However, if you prioritize shooting concerts, need independent telephoto zoom, or want more comprehensive professional. camera functions, then this isn't the right direction, at least for now. Regarding performance and battery, the iPhone Duo uses the same grade A20 Pro chip as the iPhone 11 Pro, featuring a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural Engines, and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. I will provide the Geekbench, 3DMark, and AnTuTu benchmark scores here, or you can check my database website directly. Basically, the performance is on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, so there are no surprises here. Of course, there might be some minor differences depending on the version and temperature, but it is.

# A20 Pro 性能與跑分比較

undeniably one of the best-performing phones currently available. It uses a dual-battery design for longevity; official data claims up to 31 hours of internal screen playback, 44 hours for the outer screen, and 24 hours for general usage. Looking at some current side-by-side tests, under the same 5G network conditions, some foreign media data shows the iPhone DU lasts about 13 hours and 20 minutes, while the other is 10 hours and 6 minutes, so it's fair to say its battery performance is quite excellent. I'll share my own test data with you all later, just wait a little longer; I just need to pull an all-nighter for it. Wired charging is.

# 續航資料與充電規格

also quite comprehensive. Using a 60W or higher power adapter that supports PPS, you can charge to 50%in about 20 minutes; for MagSafe, using a 35W or higher adapter, it takes about 30 minutes to reach 50%. It currently offers the best charging speed from Apple, which is sufficient, but since you're buying such an expensive phone, you still have to prepare the charger separately; that point remains the same . That wraps up today’s full review of the iPhone DU. To summarize, the iPhone DU is Apple's first. foldable iPhone. To be honest, it's not the lightest, not the thinnest, nor is it.

# 優缺點總結：誰適合買 iPhone Duo？

the foldable with the most complete camera specs, but the point is that it integrates iPhone usage habits, the Apple ecosystem, the A20 Pro, and iOS 27 into this foldable device, so the main point is that Apple users finally have a foldable; you can use a foldable now, how important is that? As for the inner screen, the original matte screen protector is very distinctive. To put it this way, if you like it, you'll love it; if you don't, you won't. In a word, it’s great for reading with much less reflection, the reading experience is fantastic, and the. protector makes the crease much less noticeable when the screen is on. Even the hinge feel and the overall build quality have been maintained at a high standard. The lack of a dedicated telephoto lens is a major drawback, but the iPhone DU’s dual-side preview, smart shooting, and dual-facing capture really fit this usage style, allowing for more ways to play. The downsides are obvious: at 250 grams, it’s not exactly light; folded at 11.3 mm, it’s not thin; you still have to get used to the ID design; the global version only has one SIM; and app compatibility will take some time to. see if the apps you use support it. If you are an iPhone user who has always wanted a larger iPhone but doesn't want to leave iOS, Apple Watch, AirPods, or iCloud, then the iPhone DU is currently the most direct foldable choice. So, if you were to ask me which form factor I prefer right now? The small ones are good-looking and convenient, more like fashion accessories—no, more like fashion phones. The traditional large ones are the most mature phone-and-tablet hybrids today, and the tri-folds are the most impressive, but their weight, price, and structural complexity make them daunting choices. As for the foldables, I believe they are the most likely to be accepted by. the general public. They are relatively small when folded, look like a phone when closed, and offer a more practical large screen when opened, providing balanced support for everything from multimedia work to entertainment.   • 從使用過三十多款摺疊手機的長期使用者角度，檢視蘋果首款摺疊 iPhone 的設計與實際特色。
  • 詳細說明摺疊手機的不同類型，並解析寬幅摺疊設計、螢幕比例與使用情境。
  • 深入分享內螢幕的霧面處理、摺痕表現與螢幕保護貼注意事項，提供實用的使用建議。
  • 整理 Touch ID、eSIM 等與日常操作相關的取捨，幫助讀者理解這款新機的優缺點。

摘要

摺疊手機類型與 iPhone 的定位

作者表示，自己使用過三十多款摺疊手機，因此這次不只開箱，也會以長期使用者的角度檢視蘋果的首次嘗試。他先將市場上的摺疊手機分成幾類：主打輕巧與趣味操作的上下翻蓋型、展開後兼具手機與平板用途的書本式大摺疊，以及藉由兩個轉軸帶來更大螢幕、但通常更厚重昂貴的三摺疊。此外，還有螢幕比例較寬、較接近平板形狀的寬幅摺疊。

這款 iPhone 採用寬幅大摺疊設計，合起時為 5.4 吋外螢幕，展開後則是 7.6 吋的小型平板。作者將它視為蘋果風格的寬幅摺疊機，而非小型翻蓋手機或單純放大的 iPhone。

機身規格與螢幕特色

機身提供星光白與夜空黑兩種顏色，容量從 256GB 到 2TB。外觀採用鈦金屬邊框與轉軸外蓋，搭配不同世代的 Ceramic Shield，並具備 IP68 防塵防水能力。手機展開厚度為 5.2 毫米、摺疊厚度為 11.3 毫米，重量 254 克；作者認為展開時相當纖薄，但收起後的厚度與重量放在口袋裡會很有存在感。

內外螢幕皆支援最高 120Hz ProMotion，戶外峰值亮度可達 3000 尼特。內螢幕採用 Super Retina XDR 可摺疊 OLED 面板，解析度為 1878 × 2670。作者特別提到螢幕上的奈米紋理霧面處理，但澄清這項效果是透過原廠預先貼上的保護貼實現，而非直接蝕刻在摺疊面板上。

霧面保護貼與摺痕表現

作者認為霧面螢幕較不易反光，長時間閱讀文章、漫畫或瀏覽網頁時相當舒適；不過，觀看暗色影片時，黑色可能不如亮面螢幕深邃，對比感也較弱，因此霧面與亮面各有適合的內容情境。

原廠保護貼讓中央摺痕在視覺上幾乎難以察覺，作者稱其摺痕表現非常出色，甚至可說是目前頂尖水準之一。雖然關閉螢幕並從斜角觀看時，仍看得到結構變化，手指也能摸到輕微隆起，但螢幕亮起後看影片、照片或瀏覽網頁，摺痕很容易被忽略。作者提醒，若內螢幕保護貼翹起，應立即聯絡原廠更換，不建議一般使用者自行撕除或更換，以免受力不均增加螢幕損壞風險。

隱藏式鏡頭與解鎖方式

內螢幕前鏡頭採用螢幕下鏡頭技術，正面觀看時隱藏得相當自然，閱讀、看影片或玩遊戲時能維持完整的沉浸感。作者原本擔心蘋果會限制內螢幕自拍功能，但實際上自拍畫質不差，也能正常使用。

由於摺疊手機會以不同方向握持，這款 iPhone 將 Touch ID 整合在側邊電源鍵，沒有 Face ID。作者表示，習慣從 iPhone X 以來 Face ID 體驗的使用者，初次改用指紋解鎖可能會覺得稍慢；他建議依使用習慣登錄左右手的多根手指，以便在桌面或手持時都能快速解鎖。全球版則僅支援 eSIM，沒有實體 SIM 卡槽，可儲存多組 eSIM、同時使用兩組門號，但更換門號仍需向電信業者辦理。影片最後開始轉向討論摺疊手機是否真正實用，但字幕在這個問題尚未展開前便中止。

Hey everyone, it’s A-Hui, I’m here! Apple's first foldable iPhone, the iPhone is finally here. Before officially introducing the star, let’s talk about the main.

# 小摺、大摺、三摺與寬摺疊怎麼選

categories in the current foldable smartphone market. The first is the " clamshell," a flip-style phone. Examples include Samsung’s Z Flip series. It’s compact when folded, usually has a stylish design, and opens up to a standard phone size. The main points are better portability and the fun new ways to use it. Second, the " large fold," which is the book-style foldable. This is currently one of the most mainstream foldable designs. When closed, it's like a phone; open it up,. and you get a 7 to 8-inch inner display . Simply put, it combines a phone and tablet into one, ideal for reading, working, multitasking, and editing. The third type is the "tri-fold." It uses two hinges, which could be inward or outward folding, and opens up to offer a large screen experience close to a tablet. The experience is honestly incredibly immersive, even approaching a laptop-like use case. You can open it up and pair it with a keyboard and mouse, similar to a laptop setup,. though it’s usually heavier, thicker, and, most importantly, more expensive. The iPhone we're looking at today, along with the previous Honor Magic V2, features a newer aspect ratio, which I would classify as a "wide fold" or " squat fold," as many people commonly call it. Essentially, they are still book-style foldables, but when closed, they have a wider, shorter aspect ratio . When opened, they are closer to a traditional tablet shape, making them better for viewing, gaming, and multimedia—it's a newer, more. practical ratio. Now, this iPhone 2 features a 5.4-inch outer display when closed, and when opened, it turns into a 7.6-inch small tablet. The first foldable phone Apple delivered today is not a small flip model, nor is it just a larger iPhone; you could call it an Apple-style wide-format large foldable. The iPhone colors this time come in Starlight White and Night Sky, or simply put, white and black to make it easier. It also comes in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and the 2TB version that I can't.

# 外觀、材質、重量與握持感

even afford. As for the exterior, it uses a titanium frame and hinge cover. The frame actually looks quite like stainless steel; the front screen is Ceramic Shield Gen 2, while the back is Gen 1, so the protection is quite perfect. It also carries an IP68 dust and water resistance rating, which for official specs means it can stay in up to 6 meters of water for 30 minutes, which is quite okay. The thickness of the iPhone is 5.2 mm when unfolded and 11.3 mm folded, weighing 254 grams; the. 5.2 mm unfolded is very thin, but folded, the 11.3 mm plus 254 grams will definitely be felt in your pocket. It has a very noticeable presence. Anyway, the 5.4-inch outer screen has a relatively short and stout aspect ratio for a wide foldable, and if we compare it to its sibling, the 18 Pro Max, it's actually even a bit wider. Whether it's a wide foldable or the iPhone we're talking about today, the screen is actually one of the most unique highlights. Regarding both its ratio and the technology used, once opened,.

# 內外螢幕與奈米紋理霧面處理

it's a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR foldable OLED screen with a resolution of 1878 by 2670. The outer screen, when folded, is a 5.4-inch Super Retina XDR display. Both internal and external screens support ProMotion technology with a refresh rate of up to 120Hz, and peak outdoor brightness can reach 3000 nits. What’s more special about the screen is—wow, it really looks great when opened—it adopts a nano-texture surface treatment, which has appeared on top-tier iPad Pro and MacBook Pro models, though they are all very. expensive and I've never used them either. The effect is that it provides better anti-reflective performance, and at the same time, it brings, hey, do you see this, it offers a better visual performance in hiding the crease. That said, I have to point out that the nano-texture treatment on this inner screen is different from computer monitors or laptops; it is actually achieved through the factory-installed screen protector, rather than being etched directly onto the foldable panel itself. This is something that needs to be clarified. Honestly, while there has been some controversy in past.

# 原廠保護貼的原理與更換提醒

discussions, I don't see any issue with the screen protector approach. Every manufacturer applies a screen protector to the inner display before it leaves the factory, so this is standard practice. As for this protector, no manufacturer recommends that users peel it off themselves. Or replace it; of course, if you’re daring enough and have a specific reason to handle it yourself, DIY replacement isn't strictly impossible. I used to replace my own screen protectors in the past, but I still do not recommend that the average user attempt to replace it on their own right now. The only thing I must remind you of is that if you notice your inner screen protector. starting to lift due to long-term use or other reasons, please contact the manufacturer immediately to have it replaced. This applies to all brands, because if the protector lifts and you continue to fold and unfold the device without addressing it......you risk increasing the likelihood of screen failure due to uneven stress being applied to the display. Now, returning to the device itself, this factory-installed protector uses a matte finish, so there is much less reflection, making it better suited for long-term reading. However, I also want to remind you—based on my own experience—that matte and glossy finishes provide two different visual.

# 霧面螢幕的優點與畫質取捨

sensations. With a matte protector like this, I personally feel one negative side effect is that when viewing black areas, you might notice that it doesn't look as bright or as deep as a standard glossy screen. If you are reading articles, manga, browsing the web, or focusing on text-based content, I think this matte finish is truly excellent and very comfortable. But if you are watching video multimedia content, especially if the content is dark— like the later seasons of Game of Thrones—then in those situations, a glossy screen will perform relatively better, as blacks will look deeper and. the contrast will be more direct. On this matte screen, that matte finish might be at a slight disadvantage. Next is the screen protector, which makes the center crease visually almost invisible. I can say that with the bonus of this protector, it’s arguably the best-looking folding phone in terms of crease performance, bar none. The protector definitely deserves credit; you can only feel a slight trace when touching it, but it’s truly a top-tier performance. I don't think there's any issue with this.

# 折痕到底藏得多好？

approach; it's actually a form of screen technology. The protector is part of its panel technology, and I even think it’s a very reasonable and well-executed solution that other manufacturers could learn from. But I still need to be clear: it doesn't mean there is absolutely no crease. If you turn off the screen and look at it from a sharp angle, you can still see the structural change, and you can feel a slight bump with your finger; that will still be there. However, once the screen is on, when you’re watching videos, viewing photos, or scrolling through web pages, the crease is very easy to overlook. Right, did everyone notice something? Did you see it?

# UDC 螢幕下鏡頭與自拍體驗

What’s missing here? Yes, exactly. The inner camera uses under-display camera (UDC) technology. Aside from the fact that the nano-treatment on the screen protector has to avoid the camera area, which causes some light reflections from different angles, when you face it directly, the camera is hidden incredibly well. If no one told you, you would find it very hard to even notice its existence. When the camera isn't in use, it stays hidden. Whether you're reading, watching videos , or gaming, the level of immersion is maxed out; it’s really satisfying. And the image quality for inner-screen selfies is actually quite decent. Actually, before it launched, and even before I got my hands on it, I was constantly wondering if Apple would lock the UDC selfie function. Turns out the quality is pretty good, and Apple didn't disable the feature, so you can still use the inner screen to take selfies. Since folding phones have both inner and outer screen usage scenarios, the iPhone, like most other brands ' foldables, uses side-mounted fingerprint recognition, integrating Touch ID into the power button on the side. So, I have to mention that it.

# Touch ID 與 eSIM 使用注意

does not have Face ID. For Apple users, since the iPhone X, you’re likely very accustomed to the experience of Face ID—picking it up to unlock, and having it recognize you automatically. Switching back to using my finger on the side button feels a bit sluggish at first, I really do feel that way. Since you pick up a foldable phone in different orientations, I suggest registering fingers from both your left and right hands; I’ve registered my left index finger, and my right thumb and index finger. You can set it up according to your needs, and the benefit is that whether it’s on the. table or in your hand, in any scenario, a quick touch is all it takes to unlock . But I have to say, since it only has Touch ID and doesn't offer face unlock or even iris scanning, that’s a bit of a shame. Also, note that the global version of the iPhone Fold only supports eSIM, so there is no physical SIM tray. It can store multiple eSIMs, and you can run two at once for dual-SIM functionality, but once you get it, you'll still need to visit your carrier to switch over your number. The next key point, which might even be more important than the hardware, is that for a foldable, it’s not just.

# iOS 多工、App 雙開與遊戲玩法

about the build, but whether it’s actually useful once unfolded. This iPhone Fold runs on a redesigned iOS 17 , where you can use split-view mode to display two apps side-by-side on the inner screen. Currently, it supports side-by-side display in landscape mode; you can have your photo app on the left and mail on the right, dragging photos directly into emails, or even open two windows of the same app, which is very practical for work. You can have an email open on one side and Excel on the other to organize data, or if you need to reply to messages while checking. reports, this split-screen method is much smoother than constantly switching apps on a regular iPhone. If the app supports it, you can even open two instances of the same program, and apps like Safari already support this. You can have one webpage open on the left and another on the right, checking product specs while looking at prices, or researching hotels while viewing maps and flight info. For users who need to look up information and multitask, this large-screen productivity is truly convenient, and it’s the main reason I’ve been using foldable phones for so many years . Even in gaming, you can apply this method for more ways to play. For. example, you can open Pikmin on the left and Pokémon on the right. That’s right, it’s super awesome— a total nerd’s dream come true. You can also have a game running on one side while looking up a strategy guide on the other. With the iPhone Du’s large unfolded screen, running two games or apps at once isn't just cool and flashy; it’s genuinely practical, spacious, and great for multitasking. I feel that the difference between foldables and tablets isn't just about having a bigger screen. If you only wanted a larger display, you’d just pick a tablet; you already have a big screen there, but foldables are different. You get the portability of a. phone combined with a massive internal screen and more versatile multitasking workflows, all packed into one pocketable device. It's super. Beyond just app multitasking, many features unique to foldables have also appeared on the iPhone. For example, you can leave it half-folded on a table. If the app supports it, like the camera or video player, it has a dedicated interface that splits automatically. You can stand it up for video calls or just leave it on the desk to use the StandBy clock feature. That's right,.

# 半摺模式與 StandBy 桌面時鐘

the most expensive desk clock ever. Perhaps because of the larger screen, this iPhone Du is the first iPhone to natively support a stylus; the Apple Pencil USB-C is supported on the iPhone Du. And it's not just for the inner screen when unfolded; both the inner and outer displays support the Apple Pencil, which is actually very rare to see right now. Whether it's the iPhone Du’s outer screen when folded or the 7.6-inch large screen when opened, you can use it for taking notes, drawing, or marking up content. You can quickly jot down an idea on the outer screen, then open it up to organize it on the big display, or use it to annotate photos, documents, and emails. So this.

# Apple Pencil 支援與功能限制

Apple Pencil utility isn't just for tablet mode; it works in both folded and unfolded states. However, it is a bit of a pity that there are still a few drawbacks. The first is that it only supports the Apple Pencil USB-C version, which lacks pressure sensitivity. So, when you draw lines, you won't get the variable line thickness you'd see with the Apple Pencil Pro. If you're a professional artist or designer with those advanced needs, that’s definitely a downside. Also, the official announcement stated this feature would launch later this year and wouldn't support floating windows. However, you can already get a sneak peek in the current open beta. If. you have it, you can update and use it right now, so I think it's coming along very quickly and should be available to everyone soon. However, this brings up a more realistic issue, which is the optimization of apps; the level of support still takes time. For now, Apple's own apps or those that have already been updated make full use of both the inner and outer screen space. But some older apps might still show black bars or appear in a windowed format. You can try to force full screen, but it’s not perfect. Plus,.

# App 適配、黑邊與軟體生態

because the UI has been moved to the right side, there will inevitably be some black bars. Take common apps: Facebook supports it, but X doesn't. Nvidia supports it, but Disney + doesn't. This just goes to show that it still takes time. So, as it stands, the iPhone Duo has hardware that is already complete, while the software ecosystem is playing catch-up for a foldable. Personally, having used many foldables, I believe Apple has much stronger leverage over app developers. Look at Facebook; it’s been six years and support is still incomplete. Six years. —do you know how painful that journey has been? It just doesn't support it; it resets every time you open it. But when Apple enters the scene, the Apple version of Facebook is ready from day one. Isn't that great? Facebook, please hurry up and update already! Even now, opening and closing it still requires a refresh. Regarding the camera, the iPhone Duo uses a 48-megapixel dual-fusion camera system with a main lens and an ultra-wide lens. The main 48-megapixel lens supports sensor-shift optical image stabilization and can achieve 2x optical-quality zoom. However, it lacks a dedicated telephoto.

# 相機規格與沒有獨立長焦的取捨

lens. This 2x zoom is based on cropping the high-resolution main sensor; it isn't the true, dedicated telephoto found on the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, so the zoom still falls a bit short. Also, since it's not a "Pro" model, it naturally lacks Pro controls and doesn't feature the latest variable aperture found on the 18 Pro Max. So, if I had to define its camera tier using a model everyone is familiar with , I’d say the overall hardware capability of the iPhone Duo is roughly on par with the standard iPhone 17. Simply put, if your daily photography needs are met by a flagship-level main lens, ultra-wide angle, and video capabilities, this is for you. However,. it’s not a complete camera system like the Pro models that include telephoto lenses or variable apertures. But its video capabilities are still very strong; the main lens supports 4K at a world-leading 120 FPS, and it also supports dual-camera simultaneous recording. The main, really the main focus of the iPhone, lies in the new features unique to its foldable form factor. For example, its dual-screen preview feature allows the person being photographed to see your composition directly through the outer display. In practice, when you're using the rear camera to take photos of someone else, they don't just have to stand there waiting for you to hit the shutter. They can check the outer screen to see if they're fully in the frame, if their.

# 雙面預覽：被拍的人也能看構圖

expression is natural, or if their pose or the composition needs adjusting. That's right, I'm talking about that boyfriend or husband of yours who really can't take a decent photo; this feature will be an absolute lifesaver for you. You can ensure that while you're being photographed, you can see the screen yourself to confirm the composition is perfect before the other person presses the shutter. Whether you're taking family portraits, shooting outfit photos for friends, or using the main camera for portraits, this function is super useful. Now, there's another handy feature: Smart Capture. Do other phones have something similar? The closest thing seems to be gesture-activated countdown timers, but.

# 智慧拍攝：合照不用追倒數計時

this Smart Capture takes it a step further. You can stand the iPhone up on a table, turn on Smart Capture, and just fix the composition. You don't have to run back to the phone to hit the shutter, and you don't have to worry about when the countdown timer will go off. The phone automatically recognizes the people in the frame. Once everyone is in the shot and ready, it will complete the photo automatically. This is incredibly convenient for group photos, where the problem is often that someone isn't standing right or is adjusting their clothes when the timer goes off. Now, it detects when you change poses, so. you don't have to keep running back and forth. You won't have to wait until after the shot to realize someone blinked or wasn't looking at the camera . Every time someone changes their pose —like a peace sign or a shift in position—it captures a shot automatically. It's fully automatic and super convenient. Other brands should take notes, especially since it can be propped up on a table now; you don't even need a tripod. This really isn't just adding photography features to a regular phone; it's about utilizing the device's inherent folding form factor. Next, similar to the outer screen camera function mentioned earlier, there is also a feature called "Look Here." The "Look Here" feature uses the.

# 看看鏡頭與雙面 FaceTime

outer screen to display animations, effectively attracting children to look toward the camera. This "Look at the Camera" feature addresses the most common problem when photographing kids: they often don't look at the lens when you hold the phone, or the more you tell them to look here, the more they look elsewhere. This "Look at the Camera" feature shows cute animated visual prompts on the outer screen, so when kids see something on the other side of the phone, their gaze naturally shifts toward the camera lens. There really should be a cat-teaser function for taking photos of my cat. There are plenty of other features too, like support for two-way FaceTime, allowing. friends to interact and talk together. If I were to evaluate the iPhone Duo, its overall camera capability is close to the iPhone 17 base model, plus the unique ways of playing that only a foldable phone offers. Honestly speaking, it’s true that it doesn't have the most luxurious camera specs among current foldables, but it knows how to use the folding screen to solve issues like selfies, group photos, and including yourself in shots, bringing some unique Apple ingenuity. However, if you prioritize shooting concerts, need independent telephoto zoom, or want more comprehensive professional. camera functions, then this isn't the right direction, at least for now. undeniably one of the best-performing phones currently available. also quite comprehensive. It currently offers the best charging speed from Apple, which is sufficient, but since you're buying such an expensive phone, you still have to prepare the charger separately; that point remains the same . the foldable with the most complete camera specs, but the point is that it integrates iPhone usage habits, the Apple ecosystem, the A20 Pro, and iOS 27 into this foldable device, so the main point is that Apple users finally have a foldable; you can use a foldable now, how important is that? 外觀、配戴與續航

盒內包含耳機、充電盒、USB 充電線，以及三組耳塞配件。耳機採半入耳設計，無須深入耳道，外型圓潤，單耳重約 5.7 克；作者表示長時間配戴舒適、受力均衡，但實際貼合度仍會因耳形而異，可用附贈的耳翼與耳塞調整。耳機支援藍牙 5.3，搭載 12 毫米動圈單體，具備 IPX4 防潑水能力，但不可沖洗或浸水。單次充電可翻譯約三小時，搭配充電盒總計約十二小時翻譯時間；充電盒與耳機總重約 101 克。
